_about: THE NEW ACT-ONE ENEMIES (FACTIONS 11/3, VAMILY rule 302, Paolo 11/2: 'more content... new enemies, new graphics, the whole package'; laws/BOHEMIA_LAW_THE_BEASTS_ARE_LAB_MADE_AND_THE_BESTIARY_FLOOR_9_29_26.md: at least 12 factions and ~75 enemy types, every Battle Brothers archetype keeps its lesson in a Bohemia skin, act one feels medieval). ONE FILE A MODDER CAN EDIT: every row is a whole enemy type (its name on the board, its Battle Brothers lesson, the wiki row it rides on, its stats, its gear, its brain, its look), every brain is a list of behaviours the fight already reads or one of the eight new ones below, every faction is a make-up by phase, and the road table says where and when each faction walks. The fight folds this file into its own tables when it deals a board (slices/BOHEMIA_FIGHT.html ownEnemies); nothing here is typed twice. Stats are the wiki row's own numbers unless a row's 'stats' says otherwise, and every such change carries its why. Every word is draft:true (WORDS owns them); every felt number is TUNING's to move (tuned:false).
looks_note: CHARACTER 11/7 (rule 427(b), asks 286 and 238): every human type wears its own men (tools/bohemia_character_the_nine_enemies.py); looks_borrowed keeps the people it stood in before, for the record
source: records/target/bb/enemies.json (each row's 'from' is a wiki unit row, its page cited there); reference/library/grok/wiki/PAGES_ALL.tar.gz for each behaviour's page

house.name: The House
house.lesson: A formation. Shields in front, hooks behind them, crossbows behind that. Break the wall or go round it.

watch.name: The Block Watch
watch.lesson: Neighbors with pitchforks. Hurt one and he runs. Their captain calls them back, so drop him first.

keepers.name: The Keepers
keepers.lesson: Desert people. They throw an axe as you close, and one of them never stops.

water.name: The Water People
water.lesson: You do not see them until they are on you. Their needles slow you down for three turns.

coyotes.name: Coyotes
coyotes.lesson: They never fight a man standing up. They go for the hurt one and eat the dead. Leave nobody on the field.

lions.name: A Mountain Lion
lions.lesson: You do not see it until it is on the man walking alone. Then he is pinned. Walk together.

hogs.name: Hogs
hogs.lesson: They come straight in and open your legs. A man who bleeds, step him back.

camels.name: Camels
camels.lesson: Never stand next to one. It kicks every way at once. Shoot it from two tiles and it runs.

bulls.name: A Bull
bulls.lesson: It runs in a straight line and cannot turn. Step off the line, or stand behind something.

wolves.name: Dire Wolves
wolves.lesson: A pack goes round you. Keep your backs together, or they take the man on the end.
wolves.why: BEASTS 2 11/3 (rule 345 amended (b)): the dire wolves as their own party; Battle Brothers' direwolf pack (the lean flanker, the rusher's brain the wiki row carries).

hyenas.name: Cave Hyenas
hyenas.lesson: They take the weak at the edge. The hurt man and the man alone go first.
hyenas.why: BEASTS 2 11/3: the cave hyenas as their own clan; Battle Brothers' hyena (the bite that bleeds, the frenzied late).

bears.name: A Short-Faced Bear
bears.lesson: It heals every turn and throws a man over its back. Kill it fast or not at all.
bears.why: BEASTS 2 11/3 (rule 345 amended (a)(e)): the lab's Ice Age bear on Battle Brothers' unhold.

sloths.name: A Ground Sloth
sloths.lesson: Slow, it heals, and it throws whoever is beside it. Shoot it and keep moving.
sloths.why: BEASTS 2 11/3 (rule 345 amended (a)(e)): Gypsum Cave's sloth on Battle Brothers' unhold.

sabres.name: A Sabre-Tooth
sabres.lesson: It waits in the rocks, jumps the man alone and holds him down, and he bleeds.

prides.name: American Lions
prides.lesson: A pride goes round you for the weak one. Keep your backs together.

bison.name: Ancient Bison
bison.lesson: It charges in a straight line like the bull, bigger. Step off its line.

horses.name: Ice Age Horses
horses.lesson: A horse kicks every man beside it, and hurt it runs. Do not stand behind it.

teratorns.name: Teratorns
teratorns.lesson: Giant vultures. They come as a flock, circle to whoever is already hurt, and run when they are hurt. One on a body eats and gets back up. Kill them fast and leave nobody lying there.
teratorns.why: WORLD 12 11/7 (rule 431(e)(f), ask lines 516 and 517: 'just another animal we can fight'): one more beast, the coyote's own brain (scavenger), no special systems.

cheetahs.name: An American Cheetah
cheetahs.lesson: The fastest thing on the road. It runs round your line to the man at the back. It cannot take much: shoot it on the way in.
cheetahs.why: BESTIARY 11/9 (rule 440(f), the floor's 17 lab-made beasts; rule 431(f): 'just another animal we can fight'): Miracinonyx, Crypt Cave, Nevada; the direwolf's pack brain ('pride') on a light, fast body.

goats.name: Harrington's Goats
goats.lesson: They live on the roofs. One comes down off the high ground in a straight line and butts a man flat. Never stand under them.
goats.why: BESTIARY 11/9 (rule 440(f), the floor's 17 lab-made beasts; rule 431(f): 'just another animal we can fight'): Oreamnos harringtoni, Smith Creek Cave, Nevada; the bull's charge (the brain 'charger') on an animal that climbs.

stilts.name: Stilt-Legged Horses
stilts.lesson: A band of thin wild asses. They crowd one man and bite. Hurt one past half and it bolts.
stilts.why: BESTIARY 11/9 (rule 440(f), the floor's 17 lab-made beasts; rule 431(f): 'just another animal we can fight'): Haringtonhippus, Gypsum Cave, Nevada; the armed peasant's nerve (the brain 'coward').

jaguars.name: An Ice Age Jaguar
jaguars.lesson: It waits at the water where you cannot see it, jumps the man on his own and holds him down. Drink in pairs.
jaguars.why: BESTIARY 11/9 (rule 440(f), the floor's 17 lab-made beasts; rule 431(f): 'just another animal we can fight'): Panthera onca augusta, Nevada's Ice Age record; the serpent's wait and grab (the brain 'stalker').

llamas.name: Large-Headed Llamas
llamas.lesson: Ranchers keep llamas to run coyotes off a herd. These walk up and kick every man beside them, and run when they are hurt.
llamas.why: BESTIARY 11/9 (rule 440(f), the floor's 17 lab-made beasts; rule 431(f): 'just another animal we can fight'): Hemiauchenia, Tule Springs; the unhold's Sweep as the kick (the brain 'kicker').

longhorns.name: A Long-Horned Bison
longhorns.lesson: The biggest thing in the valley, horns as wide as a car. It charges in a straight line and whoever it lands on goes flat. Shoot it from the side.
longhorns.why: BESTIARY 11/9 (rule 440(f), the floor's 17 lab-made beasts; rule 431(f): 'just another animal we can fight'): Bison latifrons, Tule Springs; the Ijirok's gore (the brain 'charger').

shrub_oxen.name: Shrub-Oxen
shrub_oxen.lesson: A few heavy oxen with hooked horns. They push in all round a man and hook him open, and he bleeds. Step a bleeding man back.
shrub_oxen.why: BESTIARY 11/9 (rule 440(f), the floor's 17 lab-made beasts; rule 431(f): 'just another animal we can fight'): Euceratherium, the Lake Winnemucca caves and Tule Springs; the hyena's bleeding bite as the hook (the brain 'sounder').

dogs.name: Feral Dogs
dogs.lesson: They were pets. They come in a crowd and they bite low. Kill one and the rest still come.
dogs.why: BEASTS 2 11/3: the street's dogs as their own pack, on Battle Brothers' war dogs (wardog, warhound; the armoured one late).

rows.name: House Shield
rows.lesson_bb: THE SHIELD WALL (Battle Brothers' Footman: 'Shieldwall' on every shield, bb_all/1780_Shieldwall (20 fatigue).txt)
rows.lesson: He locks his shield with the men beside him. Each one in the wall makes the others harder to hit. Hit the end of the line, or make him swing.

stats.why: act one (the perks: the shield, nothing else; the wiki's footman carries every mastery, Battle Forged and Brawny): the wiki's footman is a mid-game soldier (70 skill, a kite shield, mail to 230); the House's first men are recruits with a car door for a shield (the wiki's wooden shield) and what a 2050 shop sells, so a conscript's skill and the low end of the armour. Measured: as the wiki's footman, two of them beat a new crew of three 13 times in 20

rows.name: House Hook
rows.lesson_bb: THE POLEARM BEHIND THE WALL (Battle Brothers' Billman: 'Hook', bb_all/1021_Hook (25 fatigue).txt: the target is pulled closer)
rows.lesson: He stands one step behind the shields and reaches over them. His hook drags your man off his line and into the wall.

stats.why: act one: the low half of the wiki's range

rows.name: House Crossbow
rows.lesson_bb: THE ARCHER LINE (Battle Brothers' Arbalester: shoot, reload, shoot, from behind the line)
rows.lesson: They stay back and all shoot the same man. Close the gap fast, or put cover between you.

rows.name: Neighbor
rows.lesson_bb: THE COWARD WHO RUNS (Battle Brothers' Armed Peasant: low resolve, the first to flee)
rows.lesson: A scared man with a pitchfork. Cut him once, hard, and he runs for home.

rows.name: Block Captain
rows.lesson_bb: THE LEADER WHO RALLIES (Battle Brothers' Militia Captain: 'Rally the Troops', bb_all/1634_Rally the Troops.txt; 'Captain', bb_all/0343_Captain.txt)
rows.lesson: He stays behind his neighbors and yells them back into the fight. Kill him and the ones who run keep running.

stats.why: act one: the low half of the wiki's range

rows.name: Feral
rows.lesson_bb: THE BERSERKER (Battle Brothers' Orc Berserker: 'Berserk', bb_all/0232_Berserk.txt: 4 AP back on a kill, once a turn)
rows.lesson: He runs straight at your weakest man and never breaks. Every kill gives him another swing. Stop him before he reaches your back line.

stats.why: a man, not an orc: the wiki's 250 hitpoints is the orc's body; ours is a big man on something, so a sergeant's hitpoints (the wiki's 100, plus a tenth), skins and furs for armour, and nothing scares him (he never wavers: that is the lesson)

rows.name: Keeper
rows.lesson_bb: THE SKIRMISHER WHO THROWS FIRST (Battle Brothers' Barbarian Thrall: throwing axes, then the cleaver)
rows.lesson: He throws an axe as you walk in, then pulls a cleaver. Do not stand in the open on the way to him.

rows.name: Cutter
rows.lesson_bb: THE AMBUSHER (Battle Brothers' nomads and goblin ambushers: they wait where you cannot see them)
rows.lesson: You cannot see him until he is two steps away or he hits you. Keep your men together.

rows.name: Needle
rows.lesson_bb: THE ONE WHO POISONS (Battle Brothers' Goblin Ambusher: 'Goblin Poison', bb_all/1576_Poisoned (Goblin) (Status Effect).txt: -1 AP, -10 initiative, -1 vision, 3 turns)
rows.lesson: The darts carry lab sedative. A hit takes a step off your man, slows him and blurs his eyes for three turns. Kill the needle before your best fighter gets tagged.

stats.why: a grown woman, not a goblin: the wiki's 40 hitpoints plus a quarter

rows.name: Bowman
rows.lesson_bb: THE ARCHER LINE (Battle Brothers' Militia Marksman, bb_all/1287_Militia Marksman.txt: the militia's bows behind its spears), on the arbalester's volley
rows.lesson: A neighbor with a hunting bow. He stays behind the others and shoots whoever comes up the street first. Close on him fast: a bow is no use in your face.

rows.name: Slinger
rows.lesson_bb: THE SKIRMISHER WHO SHOOTS FROM BEHIND (Battle Brothers' Nomad Slinger, bb_all/1453_Nomad Slinger.txt), on the arbalester's volley
rows.lesson: He stays behind the cutters and slings stones at your soft men. A sling is no use up close: run him down.

rows.name: Reaver
rows.lesson_bb: THE RAIDER (Battle Brothers' Barbarian Reaver, bb_all/0189_Barbarian Reaver.txt, two-handed; the raider's way, bb_all/0297_Brigand Raider.txt: he goes for the man his friends already hold)
rows.lesson: A big man with a two-handed mace. He goes for the man his friends are already holding and puts him down. Never leave one of yours alone against two of them.

stats.why: act one: the low half of the wiki's range

rows.name: Caller
rows.lesson_bb: THE LEADER WHO RALLIES (Battle Brothers' Barbarian Drummer, bb_all/0182_Barbarian Drummer.txt: the drum keeps the war band's nerve; 'Rally the Troops', bb_all/1634_Rally the Troops.txt)
rows.lesson: He stays behind the keepers and shouts back the ones who waver. Kill the caller first, and the ones who break keep running.

rows.name: House Sergeant
rows.lesson_bb: THE LEADER WHO RALLIES (Battle Brothers' Sergeant, bb_all/1754_Sergeant.txt: 'Rally the Troops', bb_all/1634_Rally the Troops.txt)
rows.lesson: He walks behind the House's shield wall and shouts it back into line. Drop him and the wall comes apart.

stats.why: act one: the low half of the wiki's range

rows.name: Two-Hander
rows.lesson_bb: THE GREAT SWING (Battle Brothers' Zweihander, bb_all/2250_Zweihander.txt, with a two-handed sword's Swing, bb_all/1908_Swing (30 fatigue).txt: 'Hits up to 3 targets')
rows.lesson: A House man with a two-handed blade as long as his leg. When two or more of yours stand beside him, he swings round and hits all of them and knocks them back. Never let him get beside two of your men; send one man at him, or shoot him.

stats.why: act one: the low half of the wiki's range

rows.name: Outlaw
rows.lesson_bb: THE RAIDER WHO COMES STRAIGHT IN (Battle Brothers' Nomad Outlaw, bb_all/1449_Nomad Outlaw.txt, two-handed; the charge's knock-down, bb_all/0890_Gore (20 fatigue).txt)
rows.lesson: A water man with a two-handed mallet. Across open ground he runs straight at the nearest man and knocks him flat. Stand behind cover or next to a wall, where he has no straight run at you.

stats.why: act one: the low half of the wiki's range

rows.name: Spearman
rows.lesson_bb: THE LINE THAT WAITS FOR YOU (Battle Brothers' Militia, bb_all/1284_Militia.txt, with its spear; the spearwall's lesson, bb_all/1840_Spearwall (30 fatigue).txt: they hold behind their spears)
rows.lesson: A neighbor with a spear who does not come to you. The spearmen hold their line until you close, and then they all stab together. Shoot them first, or make them come to you.

rows.name: Horn
rows.lesson_bb: THE ONE WHO BREAKS YOUR NERVE (Battle Brothers' Goblin Shaman, bb_all/0870_Goblin Shaman.txt, who fights with fear from the back; the scream, bb_all/1025_Horrific Scream (0 fatigue).txt)
rows.lesson: A kid with an air horn, staying out of reach behind the others. The blast breaks a man's nerve: he wavers, and a wavering man fights badly or runs. Shoot the horn first.

rows.name: Bruiser
rows.lesson_bb: THE ONE WHO THROWS YOU (Battle Brothers' Orc Berserker, bb_all/1492_Orc Berserker.txt, with the Unhold's Fling Back, bb_all/0794_Fling Back (20 fatigue).txt: tosses the target behind him)
rows.lesson: A heavy who grabs the nearest of your men and throws him over his shoulder, out of your line and among his friends. Keep your weak men behind someone, never beside him.

stats.why: a man, not an orc: the wiki's 250 hitpoints is the orc's body (the keepers' feral rides the same row at 110); ours a big man, 140

rows.name: Coyote
rows.lesson_bb: THE ONE THAT EATS THE DEAD (Battle Brothers' Nachzehrer: 'Gruesome Feast: eats a dead body... heals', bb_all/0925_Gruesome Feast (25 fatigue).txt; its numbers the Wolf's, bb_all/2230_Wolf.txt)
rows.lesson: Coyotes never fight a man standing up. They circle to the hurt one, run when they are hurt, and a coyote beside a body eats and gets back up. Kill them fast and leave nobody lying there.

stats.why: a coyote is 10 to 18 kg, a third of the wolf the wiki's row is: its hitpoints and nerve about half; just as quick

beast.why: the wiki's plain Bite (15-35), not the wolf's: a small dog's jaw; a coyote cannot climb a wall or a ladder

rows.roams: the suburbs' edges and the dead golf courses, every wash; more at night
rows.real: Canis latrans, in every part of the valley today (Nevada Department of Wildlife)
rows.feed: The coyotes were here before the city and they will be here after it. They eat what the fights leave.

rows.name: Mountain Lion
rows.lesson_bb: THE ONE THAT GRABS AND HOLDS (Battle Brothers' Serpent: it drags a man and coils round him, bb_all/1757_Serpent.txt; the ambush of the nomads' cutthroat)
rows.lesson: You cannot see it until it is two tiles off or it jumps. It goes for the man on his own and pins him: he cannot move until he fights his way up or it dies. One good shot drops it. Walk together.

stats.why: a 55 to 70 kg cat, faster than the wiki's serpent and with no scales (armour 10, its hide); 110 hitpoints so a rifle's good shot drops it (Paolo 9/30: a beast is never a boss)

beast.why: the serpent's own bite (50-70): the neck bite a cougar kills with; a puma jumps 4.5 m straight up and walks a roof

rows.roams: the mountain (the Spring Mountains: Mount Charleston, Red Rock's cliffs) and the hills' edges at night
rows.real: Puma concolor, resident in the Spring Mountains (Nevada Department of Wildlife)
rows.feed: Nothing let the lions out. They came down off Mount Charleston after the lab's horses and camels did.

rows.name: Feral Hog
rows.lesson_bb: THE ONE THAT OPENS YOU UP (Battle Brothers' Hyena: 'Hyena Bite... causes Bleeding... if at least 6 hitpoints were lost', bb_all/1055_Hyena Bite (6 fatigue).txt)
rows.lesson: Hogs come straight at the nearest man, low and fast, and the tusks open his legs: every hit that draws blood bleeds 5 a turn for 2 turns. Their shoulders are armoured. Step a bleeding man back.

stats.why: a boar is 60 to 150 kg and carries a cartilage shield up to 5 cm thick over its shoulders (armour 40 on the body); it does not quit (resolve 70, the hyena's 50 plus)

beast.why: the hyena's own bite (20-35, all of it on the armour) as the tusk; a pig cannot climb

rows.roams: only where there is water: the Wash, the wetlands, the lake shore, the dam
rows.real: Sus scrofa: farm pigs go wild in two generations; a pig cannot sweat and dies in the open desert in summer without a wallow
rows.feed: The pig farm north of town fed on the Strip's leftovers for fifty years. When the trucks stopped, the pigs walked to the Wash.

rows.name: Camelops
rows.lesson_bb: THE ONE THAT SWEEPS ROUND IT (Battle Brothers' Unhold: 'Sweep... can hit up to 3 targets next to each other... knockback', bb_all/1906_Sweep (20 fatigue).txt)
rows.lesson: A camel kicks with any leg, any way. One kick hits every man beside it and knocks each a tile back. It is not looking for a fight: hurt it and it runs. Shoot it from two tiles, never stand next to it.

stats.why: a 700 to 900 kg grazer, not a giant: two thirds of the unhold's hitpoints, no regeneration (a camel does not heal in a fight), and the nerve of prey (resolve 40)

beast.why: TUNING 2 11/3 (rule 370(9), Paolo: 'these big ass animals better fuck you up if they get close to you for real'): the wiki's Size 2 Headbutt (70-90, half through armour) as the kick, one blow that takes half a man in mail (was the unhold's Sweep, 40-80, which mail held to a tenth); a camel cannot climb

rows.roams: the open desert north of town: Tule Springs and Gypsum Cave, where the lab was, and the springs
rows.real: Camelops hesternus: Tule Springs bone; its DNA read from Yukon bone in 2015 (Heintzman et al.), a sister of the living camels; a dromedary surrogate
rows.feed: The lab at Tule Springs made them from the bones in the wash. They were the first thing to walk out when the power went.

rows.name: Feral Bull
rows.lesson_bb: THE ONE THAT CHARGES (Battle Brothers' Ijirok: 'Gore... has knockback and staggers the target on hit (a range of 3 to 6 tiles)', bb_all/0890_Gore (20 fatigue).txt)
rows.lesson: A bull puts its head down and runs at a man two to four tiles off in a straight line. If it lands, he goes flat and loses his next turn. It cannot turn: step off its line, or keep a wall or a man between you.

stats.why: an 800 kg bull: the unhold's weight without its regeneration; it does not run (resolve 90)

beast.why: TUNING 2 11/3 (rule 370(9), Paolo: 'these big ass animals better fuck you up if they get close to you for real'): the wiki's Gore (100-130, the Ijirok's horns) as the horns, the charge its own (numbers.charge): half a man in mail, a dead man in rags (was the unhold's Sweep, 40-80); a bull cannot climb

rows.roams: the open desert and the dead farms and fields, where the springs are
rows.real: Bos taurus: range cattle have run loose without an owner on Gold Butte, Clark County, for decades (the cattle the BLM tried to round up in 2014)
rows.feed: Gold Butte had wild cattle long before the crash. Now nobody counts them, and the bulls come down to the springs.

rows.name: Short-Faced Bear
rows.lesson_bb: THE UNHOLD (Battle Brothers: 'Regeneration will heal for 15% of their max Hitpoints at the start of each turn', bb_all/1661_Regeneration.txt; 'Fling Back will toss the target behind the unhold, target gets 10 Fatigue and suffers falling damage', bb_all/0794_Fling Back (20 fatigue).txt; 'they can use Fling Back to get close to a vulnerable brother... or kill someone with 10 HP or less', bb_all/0146_Armored Unhold.txt)
rows.lesson: The lab's bear. It heals every turn, so a slow fight is its fight: hit it all at once. It throws the man beside it over its back, and it finishes the hurt one that way. Keep the hurt man away from it.

stats.why: a 600 to 900 kg bear, long-legged and fast for its size (Arctodus): nine tenths of the unhold's hitpoints, its regeneration and its throw; quicker than the unhold (initiative 90), and a bear's nerve

beast.why: TUNING 2 11/3 (rule 370(9), Paolo: 'these big ass animals better fuck you up if they get close to you for real'): the wiki's Bite (70-110, half through armour) as the maul, its Regeneration and its Fling Back (the brain 'unhold'): half a man in mail (was the unhold's Sweep, 40-80); a 700 kg bear does not climb a wall

rows.roams: near the fossil beds: Gypsum Cave in the hills to the east and Tule Springs north of town, where the lab was
rows.real: Arctodus simus, the giant short-faced bear of the Ice Age: its mitochondrial genome read from bone (Mitchell et al. 2016); made on the brown bear (the right size: a big grizzly is 400 to 600 kg)
rows.feed: The lab kept its bears in the old prison yard. The fence was the last thing on the grid to go dark.

rows.name: Shasta Ground Sloth
rows.lesson_bb: THE UNHOLD (Battle Brothers: Regeneration, 15% of its hitpoints at the start of each turn, bb_all/1661_Regeneration.txt; Fling Back, the man beside it tossed behind it with 10 fatigue and falling damage, bb_all/0794_Fling Back (20 fatigue).txt)
rows.lesson: Slow, and it heals every turn. It throws whoever stands beside it. Shoot it from range and keep moving; never stand next to it with your back to a wall.

stats.why: a 250 to 350 kg sloth with hide full of bone (the ground sloths' osteoderms): the unhold's hitpoints and its nerve, its regeneration and its throw, and slow (initiative 40)

beast.why: TUNING 2 11/3 (rule 370(9), Paolo: 'these big ass animals better fuck you up if they get close to you for real'): the wiki's Uproot (70-100, the schrat's, half through armour) as the claws, its Regeneration and its Fling Back (the brain 'unhold'): half a man in mail (was the unhold's Sweep, 40-80); a ground sloth does not climb

rows.roams: Gypsum Cave and the canyons east of town, where its dung lay for eleven thousand years
rows.real: Nothrotheriops shastensis: Gypsum Cave, a few miles from the Strip, kept its dung, and its DNA was read from it (Poinar et al. 1998); its living kin are 4 to 8 kg tree sloths, so no mother could carry it: the lab grew it in its own womb (the lamb in the bag, CHOP 2017, made huge)
rows.feed: It came out of the canyon at Gypsum Cave, where its dung lay for eleven thousand years. It is slow. It does not stop.

rows.name: Sabre-Tooth
rows.lesson_bb: THE SERPENT'S WAIT AND GRAB WITH THE HYENA'S BLEEDING BITE (Battle Brothers: the serpent lies unseen and drags its prey, bb_all/1757_Serpent.txt; 'Hyena Bite... causes bleeding', bb_all/1055_Hyena Bite (6 fatigue).txt): no Battle Brothers beast is a sabre-tooth, so it takes the two lessons it was: it waits unseen, springs and pins, and the sabres open a man so he bleeds
rows.lesson: It waits in the rocks where you cannot see it, jumps the man on his own, holds him down and the bite makes him bleed. Never walk the rocks one at a time.

stats.why: a 160 to 280 kg cat: twice the mountain lion's hitpoints, slower than it (a heavy ambusher, not a runner), the best killer's nerve

beast.why: the serpent's bite (50-70) as the sabres, with the hyena's gash (the brain 'ambusher'); a big cat climbs a low roof

rows.roams: the rocks and the canyons: Red Rock, the Gypsum Cave hills
rows.real: Smilodon fatalis: its genome read from Ice Age bone (Paijmans et al. 2017); made on the largest living cats
rows.feed: Nobody at the lab would say how many sabre-tooths there were. The fence count was two short.

rows.name: American Lion
rows.lesson_bb: THE DIREWOLF PACK (Battle Brothers' direwolf: fast, and a pack that goes round you to the weak one, bb_all/0629_Direwolf.txt): a pride of the Ice Age lion hunts the way the wolves do, bigger
rows.lesson: A pride. Two or three come at once and go round you for the weak one. Keep your backs together.

stats.why: a 250 to 400 kg lion, a quarter over an African lion: twice the direwolf's hitpoints, a little slower, a lion's nerve

beast.why: the direwolf's bite and its pack (the brain 'pride'); a 300 kg lion does not walk a roof

rows.roams: the open desert and the hills north and east of town
rows.real: Panthera atrox, the American lion: its DNA read from Ice Age bone (Barnett et al. 2009, 2016); made on the African lion
rows.feed: The lab's lions were the show's, once. Now they hunt in threes across the desert north of town.

rows.name: Ancient Bison
rows.lesson_bb: THE ONE THAT CHARGES (Battle Brothers' Ijirok: 'Gore... has knockback and staggers the target on hit', bb_all/0890_Gore (20 fatigue).txt): the bull's charge on a heavier animal
rows.lesson: A bison puts its head down and runs at a man in a straight line, and it is bigger than the bull. Step off its line, and never stand in front of a herd.

stats.why: a 1,000 to 1,600 kg bison: the unhold's weight and more, without its regeneration; slower than the bull

beast.why: the unhold's Sweep (40-80) as the horns, the bull's charge (numbers.charge); a bison cannot climb

rows.roams: the open desert and the dead golf courses' grass, north of town
rows.real: Bison antiquus: Tule Springs bone; made on the plains bison, its own descendant
rows.feed: The bison came out of the lab's pens at Tule Springs and found the golf courses before the grass died.

rows.name: Ice Age Horse
rows.lesson_bb: THE ONE THAT SWEEPS ROUND IT (Battle Brothers' Unhold: 'Sweep... can hit up to 3 targets next to each other... knockback', bb_all/1906_Sweep (20 fatigue).txt): no Battle Brothers beast is a horse, so it takes the camel's kick: every man beside it struck and knocked back, and hurt it runs
rows.lesson: A horse kicks every man beside it and knocks him back. It is not looking for a fight: hurt it and it runs. Do not stand behind it.

stats.why: a 300 to 400 kg wild horse: a third under the camel's hitpoints, quick, and prey's nerve

beast.why: the unhold's Sweep as the kick (the brain 'kicker'); a horse cannot climb

rows.roams: the open desert and the solar fields north of town, in bands
rows.real: Equus, the valley's own Ice Age horse (Tule Springs and Gypsum Cave bone); Ice Age horse genomes read many times (the 700,000-year-old Yukon horse, Orlando et al. 2013); made on a horse
rows.feed: The lab's horses carry the freeze marks the wild horse men used to burn on their necks. Somebody here still knew how.

rows.name: Teratorn
rows.lesson_bb: THE ONE THAT EATS THE DEAD (Battle Brothers' Nachzehrer: 'Gruesome Feast: eats a dead body... heals', bb_all/0925_Gruesome Feast (25 fatigue).txt; its numbers the Wolf's, bb_all/2230_Wolf.txt), as the coyote: one more beast, no special systems (rule 431(f))
rows.lesson: Teratorns come as a flock and never fight a man standing up. They circle to the hurt one, run when they are hurt, and one beside a body eats and gets back up. Kill them fast and leave nobody lying there.

stats.why: a 15 to 25 kg bird with a four-metre span: more than a coyote's hitpoints, a little slower to start (it has to get off the ground), the same nerve; draft, TUNING's to move

beast.why: the wiki's plain Bite (15-35) as the hooked beak's tear; it walks and fights on the ground like every beast (rule 431(f): no special flight rules)

rows.roams: the open desert and the hills, the landfill and the Wash: wherever something has died
rows.real: Teratornis incredibilis, the giant teratorn, described by Hildegarde Howard (1952) from Smith Creek Cave in Nevada's own Snake Range; its cousin T. merriami (La Brea) stood about 75 cm and spanned 3.5 to 3.8 m; a California condor surrogate; about four metres of wing
rows.feed: The lab grew them in condor eggs and tagged their wings the way the condor people did. The tags still have numbers on them.

rows.name: American Cheetah
rows.lesson_bb: THE WOLFRIDER (Battle Brothers' Goblin Wolfrider: the fast one that goes round the line for the soft man at the back), on the direwolf's pack brain ('pride', bb_all/0629_Direwolf.txt) and the direwolf's bite (bb_all direwolf_bite_6)
rows.lesson: The fastest thing on the road. It runs round your line to the man at the back before you can turn. It cannot take much: one good shot on the way in and it is done. Keep your back line behind your front.

stats.why: a 60 to 95 kg runner: a third of the giant lion's hitpoints, the quickest start in the valley, a coward's hide; draft, TUNING's to move

beast.why: the direwolf's bite (30-50): a cat's throat bite at a sprint; a runner's long legs are not a climber's

rows.roams: the open flats: the airport's runways, the freeway's straight miles, the dry lake beds
rows.real: Miracinonyx trumani, the 'American cheetah': its first skull from Crypt Cave, Nevada (Orr 1969); its DNA read (mitochondrial 2005; nuclear genomes 2026: a puma's cousin built to run); made on a puma
rows.feed: The lab grew them in cougars. The cougars could not keep up with what they gave birth to.

rows.name: Harrington's Goat
rows.lesson_bb: THE ONE THAT CHARGES (Battle Brothers' Ijirok: 'Gore... has knockback and staggers the target on hit', bb_all/0890_Gore (20 fatigue).txt) from the high ground: a goat climbs (rule 321) and butts with the wiki's Headbutt (size_1_headbutt_15)
rows.lesson: Goats live on the roofs. One comes down off the high ground in a straight line and butts a man flat; he loses his next turn. Step off its line, and never stand under it.

stats.why: a 60 to 80 kg goat with a skull built for butting (a little head armour); quick; draft, TUNING's to move

beast.why: the wiki's Headbutt (35-45) as the horns; a mountain goat walks a cliff, so a roof is nothing

rows.roams: the hills and the rock: Frenchman Mountain, the Sheep Range, the cliffs over the springs
rows.real: Oreamnos harringtoni, Harrington's mountain goat: named from Smith Creek Cave, Nevada (Stock 1936); its DNA read (Campos et al. 2010); made on a mountain goat
rows.feed: Somebody saw the goats on the roof of the Stratosphere's old ticket booth. Nobody saw how they got up there.

rows.name: Stilt-Legged Horse
rows.lesson_bb: THE COWARD WHO RUNS (Battle Brothers' Armed Peasant: low resolve, the first to flee; the brain 'coward' runs below half), on the wiki's plain Bite (bite_0) as a burro's teeth
rows.lesson: A band of thin wild asses. They crowd round one man and bite. Hurt one past half and it bolts. Hurt them hard, one at a time.

stats.why: a 200 kg wild ass: under the Ice Age horse's hitpoints, as quick, prey's nerve; draft, TUNING's to move

beast.why: the wiki's plain Bite (15-35): a donkey fights a dog with its teeth and its front feet; a horse cannot climb

rows.roams: the open desert and the solar fields, in bands, where the wild burros already were
rows.real: Haringtonhippus francisci, the stilt-legged horse: its most complete skull from Gypsum Cave, Nevada, and its DNA read from that skull (Heintzman et al. 2017); made on a burro
rows.feed: The burros in the solar fields had foals that were not burros. Long legs, longer than they should be. The lab paid the ranchers not to talk.

rows.name: Ice Age Jaguar
rows.lesson_bb: THE ONE THAT GRABS AND HOLDS (Battle Brothers' Serpent: it waits, drags a man and coils round him, bb_all/1757_Serpent.txt), the mountain lion's way, at the water
rows.lesson: It waits at the water where you cannot see it, jumps the man on his own and holds him down until he fights free or it dies. Drink in pairs.

stats.why: a 120 to 150 kg cat, a fifth over a jaguar: near the sabre-tooth's hitpoints, its nerve; draft, TUNING's to move

beast.why: the serpent's bite (50-70): the jaguar kills with a bite to the skull; a jaguar climbs trees and roofs

rows.roams: the Wash and the lake's shore: a water cat, it swims
rows.real: Panthera onca augusta, the Ice Age jaguar: Nevada among its records (Kurten 1973); jaguar mitogenomes read from Ice Age bone; made on a jaguar
rows.feed: Fishermen at the Wash stopped going out at dusk. One of them says it came up out of the water.

rows.name: Large-Headed Llama
rows.lesson_bb: THE ONE THAT SWEEPS ROUND IT (Battle Brothers' Unhold: 'Sweep... can hit up to 3 targets next to each other... knockback', bb_all/1906_Sweep (20 fatigue).txt), the camel's kick on its long-legged cousin
rows.lesson: Ranchers keep llamas to run coyotes off a herd. These walk straight up to a stranger and kick every man beside them, knocking each one back. Hurt one and it runs. Never stand next to it.

stats.why: a 200 to 300 kg llama: under the horse's hitpoints, as quick, a guard's nerve; draft, TUNING's to move

beast.why: the unhold's Sweep as the kick (the brain 'kicker'), as the camel's and the horse's; a llama cannot climb a wall

rows.roams: the open desert, the golf courses and the foothills, in strings
rows.real: Hemiauchenia, the large-headed llama: Tule Springs (the monument's one forelimb bone); Ice Age, so its DNA is readable (not yet read); made on a llama
rows.feed: A rancher out by Moapa bought llamas to keep the coyotes off. Now nothing comes near his place. Including him.

rows.name: Long-Horned Bison
rows.lesson_bb: THE ONE THAT CHARGES (Battle Brothers' Ijirok: 'Gore... has knockback and staggers the target on hit', bb_all/0890_Gore (20 fatigue).txt): the bison's charge on the biggest animal in the valley
rows.lesson: The biggest thing in the valley. Its horns are as wide as a car. It charges in a straight line and whoever it lands on goes flat. Never stand in front of it; shoot it from the side.

stats.why: 1,800 to 2,000 kg, twice a bison: a third over the ancient bison's hitpoints, slower to start; draft, TUNING's to move

beast.why: the wiki's Gore (100-130, stagger and knockback) as the horns, as the bull's; a bison cannot climb

rows.roams: the open desert and the dead golf courses' grass
rows.real: Bison latifrons, the giant long-horned bison: Tule Springs (the monument lists it, 'cf.'); its mitogenome read (Froese et al. 2017, the Snowmass bone); made on the plains bison
rows.feed: The lab only ever made three of the big ones. People have counted four.

rows.name: Shrub-Ox
rows.lesson_bb: THE ONE THAT OPENS YOU UP (Battle Brothers' Hyena: 'Hyena Bite... causes Bleeding... if at least 6 hitpoints were lost', bb_all/1055_Hyena Bite (6 fatigue).txt) as the hooked horns, on the wiki's Headbutt (size_1_headbutt_15)
rows.lesson: A few heavy oxen with horns that hook down past the eyes. They push in all round a man and hook him open; every hit that draws blood bleeds. Step a bleeding man back.

stats.why: a 600 kg ox with a horn boss over its skull (head armour): near the camel's hitpoints, slow; draft, TUNING's to move

beast.why: the wiki's Headbutt (35-45) as the hooking horns, the hog's bleed (the brain 'sounder'); an ox cannot climb

rows.roams: the brush on the hills and the desert's washes: it eats the shrubs
rows.real: Euceratherium, the shrub-ox: the Lake Winnemucca caves (Nevada) and a bovid its size at Tule Springs; Ice Age, so its DNA is readable (not yet read); made on a muskox
rows.feed: The lab grew the shrub-oxen in muskox cows flown down from the north. The cows died in the first summer. The calves did not.

water._why: BEASTS 2 11/3 (rule 359, the cheap clone, Paolo 11/3: 'I know water is important too'; laws/BOHEMIA_LAW_THE_CHEAP_CLONE_11_3_26.md s3): the Mojave gets about four inches of rain a year, so every beast lives where the water is, and the water is where the people are: a beast in the street came for a pool. This is which beast lives at which water, for WORLD [creatures] to put them there. kinds are the valley's waters; by_faction lists each beast party's waters, the first the one it is found at most; drinks is the real animal's need (draft, sourced in the record). draft: WORLD places, TUNING weighs.

kinds.wash: the Wash: the city's treated water ran to Lake Mead at about 200 million gallons a day; after the crash thinner and dirtier, the valley's biggest river of beasts
kinds.lake_shore: Lake Mead's receded shore and its mud
kinds.springs: the springs: Tule Springs, Corn Creek, Red Rock's seeps, the old springs where the city began, Gypsum Cave's seeps
kinds.guzzlers: the guzzlers: the state's old wildlife water tanks in the desert, built for the bighorn sheep
kinds.pools: the backyard pools, tens of thousands of them

wolves.drinks: a pack drinks every day or two; it travels between waters

hyenas.drinks: a hyena drinks when it can and goes days without; the clan sits by the city's edge water

dogs.drinks: a dog needs water every day: the street's pools and broken mains

coyotes.drinks: a coyote gets much of its water from its food; it comes to the pools at night

lions.drinks: a cat gets most of its water from its kill and waits at the water for the rest

hogs.drinks: a pig cannot sweat: it needs a wallow every hot day, so it never leaves the water

camels.drinks: a camel goes a week or more without and then drinks over 100 litres at once

bulls.drinks: a bull drinks 40 to 80 litres a day: it never ranges far from a spring

bears.drinks: a bear drinks daily and eats at the water's edge

sloths.drinks: Gypsum Cave's sloth ate the desert's plants by the cave's seeps; it stays near them

sabres.drinks: an ambusher at the water: it waits where the others come to drink

prides.drinks: a pride follows the herds to the water and hunts them there

bison.drinks: a bison drinks 30 to 40 litres a day, once a day, in a herd

horses.drinks: a horse drinks 25 to 45 litres a day and walks to water every day or two

teratorns.drinks: a condor drinks and bathes at open water every day or two and flies far between waters; a teratorn the same, on a bigger wing

cheetahs.drinks: a cat gets most of its water from its kill and drinks at the tanks between runs

goats.drinks: the bighorn's guzzlers: a goat drinks at the rock tanks every day or two in the heat

stilts.drinks: a burro can lose a quarter of its body's water and drink it back in five minutes

jaguars.drinks: a jaguar is a water cat: it swims, and hunts what comes to drink

llamas.drinks: a llama drinks little and gets most of its water from green browse

longhorns.drinks: a bison drinks 30 to 40 litres a day; this one twice that

shrub_oxen.drinks: a browser of the brush at the seeps; it never strays far from them

shieldwall.quote: Doubles Melee Defense and Ranged Defense shield stats for 1 turn (including the Shield Expert perk bonus). Grants additional +5 Melee Defense and +5 Ranged Defense for each adjacent ally using the Shieldwall

hooker.quote: +10% chance to hit, target is pulled closer to user

volley.quote: the backline of the Noble House line; FACTIONS: they all shoot the man the first bolt hit

coward.quote: the wiki's 35 resolve; FACTIONS: under half his hitpoints he runs, once

rallier.quote: Rally the Troops; FACTIONS: he calls a man back the moment he wavers, not only when he breaks

berserker.quote: Once per turn, upon killing an enemy, 4 Action Points are immediately regained

thrower.quote: the thrall's bundle of throwing axes, then the cleaver

ambusher.quote: FACTIONS: unseen until a man of yours stands within lurk.seen_within tiles or he strikes

scavenger.quote: Eats a dead body, grows in size (if possible), improves its morale, removes all injuries and heals; FACTIONS: a coyote beside a body eats while it is hurt; under a third of its hitpoints it runs, once

stalker.quote: FACTIONS: unseen until a man of yours is lurk.seen_within tiles off or it strikes; while unseen it moves only to a tile it can spring from this turn, else it lies still; it goes round for the weakest; the man it lands on is pinned (the net's rule) until he gets up or it is gone

sounder.quote: causes Bleeding for 5 dmg per turn... if at least 6 hitpoints were lost from the attack. Bleeding lasts 2 turns.

kicker.quote: Sweep does knockback, will stagger the target, can hit up to 3 targets next to each other; FACTIONS: a camel's kick reaches every man beside it, and under half its hitpoints it runs

ambusher.quote: BEASTS 2 11/3: the sabre-tooth: the serpent's wait, spring and pin (the mountain lion's 'stalker') with the hyena's bleeding bite (the hog's 'gashes')

pride.quote: BEASTS 2 11/3: the American lion's pride hunts as Battle Brothers' direwolf pack: surround, the weak one first

unhold.quote: Regeneration; Fling Back; Sweep. They prefer fighting with a regular attack, but can use Fling Back to get close to a vulnerable brother, take the high ground, cancel a shieldwall, or kill someone with 10 HP or less (BEASTS 2 11/3: the short-faced bear and the Shasta ground sloth)

charger.quote: Gore... has knockback and staggers the target on hit (has a range of 3 to 6 tiles)

raider.quote: If armed with a long weapon like Pike and there are no enemies nearby, they wait to not get ahead of their melee allies.
raider.why: BESTIARY 11/10 (rule 443(d), the routine 'enemy types and factions'): ai.json's own raider (the brigand raider's way), named here so a keeper can ride it; no new key

great_swing.quote: Hits up to 3 targets counterclockwise; BESTIARY 11/11: the House greatsword swings at every man beside him (the fight's kick, numbers.kick), never a beast's

runner_in.quote: Gore... has knockback and staggers the target on hit; BESTIARY 11/11: the outlaw's straight run and knock-down (the fight's charge, numbers.charge) on a man

spear_line.quote: the spearwall's lesson: they hold behind their spears until you close (the fight's hold_line), then fight as one line

horn.quote: BESTIARY 11/14: the kids' horn screams as the geist does (racial_skills.json by_enemy.kids_horn), from out of reach

thrower_back.quote: Fling Back tosses the target behind; BESTIARY 11/14: the heavies' bruiser, the first man who throws (the fight's fling, numbers.fling)

shieldwall.quote: 4 AP, 20 fatigue; doubles the shield's defences for a turn; +5 for each adjacent ally using it. near_tiles is ours: he raises it when a foe is that close

hook.quote: 6 AP, 25 fatigue, +10% chance to hit, target is pulled closer to user; target_fatigue is ours (the page's number is cut off in the library)

lurk.quote: he shows when a man of yours is two tiles away, or the moment he strikes; wait_rounds (FIVE MORE BEASTS): the lion lies still that many of its turns waiting for a man to come within its spring, then stalks in

gash.quote: Bleeding for 5 dmg per turn on Hyenas... if at least 6 hitpoints were lost from the attack. Bleeding lasts 2 turns.

kick.quote: the Sweep's own 4 AP and 20 fatigue (beast_attacks.json sweep_20); FACTIONS: every man beside it, not three, because a camel kicks with any leg

charge.quote: Gore: 6 AP, 20 fatigue, knockback, staggers, a range of 3 to 6 tiles; FACTIONS: 2 to 4 of ours (a tile is a house), +10 to hit for the run (ours, draft)

regenerate.quote: Regeneration will heal for 15% of their max Hitpoints at the start of each turn

fling.quote: 4 AP, 20 fatigue: Fling Back will toss the target behind the unhold, target gets 10 Fatigue and suffers falling damage. The falling damage (5 to 10) is ours (the page gives no number), finish_hp is the unhold's page ('kill someone with 10 HP or less'), chance is ours: how often it throws a man it cannot finish (draft, TUNING's)

feed.quote: Gruesome Feast: 6 AP, 25 fatigue; eats a dead body... heals; FACTIONS: 25 hitpoints a bite, two bites a body (ours, draft)

count_scale_beasts_why: a coyote pack is as many as his crew; a mountain lion hunts alone (one, two at eight or more); a hog sounder is 2 to 4 against a new crew (0.8 lost 9 of 10 to a crew of 6, the new-enemies gate's SIZED TO THE CREW, measured 11/3); a camel herd is a few; a bull is one, two at a big crew (FACTIONS 11/3, draft, TUNING's to move)

waiting._about: BESTIARY 11/10 (rule 443(d), rule 441: no stand-in art where finished art is owed): BUILT AND WAITING FOR ITS CLOTHES, as the bison waited for room. The flock is Battle Brothers' cultists as the trailer park's people; its party, its row, its make-up, its sizing (0.8: a new crew of 3 beats it 8 in 10, of 6 10 in 10, AUTO) and its road are below and go into the live tables the moment it has its own clothes. Every dressed look left is someone else's: person_town_* are his company (ours.people_looks.crew, CHARACTER 11/10), person_woman_* his followers (retinue.json), faction_homeless/caravans/volunteers the bosses' crews (boss_act_one.json), person_rare_* the rare hires, cast_* the cast. CHARACTER owns the garments (rule 427(b)); the ask is in handoffs/CHARACTER.md. The looks below were the first cut and are NOT to ship: they are his company's.

flock.name: The Flock
flock.lesson: They do not run. The people nobody counts come at you together, and every one of them keeps coming until it falls.
flock.why: BESTIARY 11/10 (rule 443(d)): Battle Brothers' cultists (bb_all/0477_Cultist (Enemy).txt) as the trailer park's people; factions.json's 'The flock'.

rows.name: Faithful
rows.lesson_bb: THE ONES WHO DO NOT RUN (Battle Brothers' Cultist, bb_all/0477_Cultist (Enemy).txt: the faithful's family lesson, 'They do not run'), on the berserker's rush
rows.lesson: The flock: people nobody counts, with whatever they could carry. They never run. Every one of them comes at you until it falls, so fight them where only a few can reach you at once.

stats.why: the wiki's cultist (60 hitpoints, 80 resolve) with no nerve to break; act one: the low half of the wiki's armour

champions._about: BESTIARY 11/10 (rule 443(d), the routine 'enemy types and factions'): CHAMPIONS ARE RARE NAMED MEN (Battle Brothers: a band can carry one named man, its toughest, the champion rows of records/target/bb/enemies.json). A band dealt one of these kinds (a party's mix, at its own act weight: rare by the mix) carries him under his own name and title; his fall is HELD BREATH (the fight's CUT_SAYS). The names are drafts for WORDS; the rule is the fight's own.

road.why: Paolo: 'Battle Brothers... how many groups are moving around at a certain time... way more'; enemies are never forced (a party you can see and avoid). A roaming party takes its faction from the act (by_act, added to COMBAT's road_factions), from the ground it walks (the faction that holds that ground in records/target/bb/factions.json walks there district_mult times as often) and from the hour (night).
road.night_why: the block watch goes home after dark; the water people and the keepers move at night (draft). FIVE MORE BEASTS: coyotes and lions hunt at night (a puma is most active from dusk to dawn); hogs go night-active in the heat; camels bed down
